references.text: Moses asks for God's name when he is to speak to Pharaoh, corresponding to his complaint about speaking in God's name
Moses' first meeting with Pharaoh where he speaks in the Lord's name, which led to Pharaoh worsening the situation of the Israelites
Pharaoh's response to Moses' message - he increased the labor burden and made things worse for the people
God's answer to Moses' complaint - He will force Pharaoh to let the people go free
God's promise to Abraham that his descendants would be oppressed, but that He would deliver them
Jeremiah also complains to God that his service seems to have made the situation worse
Job complains to God that he receives no answer or deliverance, similar to Moses' frustration
Clear narrative and theological connection within the same Exodus saga; 7:4 explains God's purpose with the 'evils' that Moses complains about in 5:23.
Nehemiah 9:10 provides the theological interpretive key to Moses' doubt in Exodus 5:23 by confirming God's purpose behind the actions against Pharaoh.
Narrative contrast: God's commission in 3:10 meets Moses' doubt about the outcome in 5:23.
